docs.title: > A personal correction system built from experience—not...
docs.text:
> A personal correction system built from experience—not from universal ideas of right and wrong. When something happens that I don’t like, I ask myself what I would rather have done and write it down as what I should’ve done instead. For every mistake there is a right move, so each line pairs the thing I did with the thing I’ll do next time. These reminders are specific to me: my situations, my preferences, and what I want to avoid repeating. What works for me may not work for someone else.
> 
- I should’ve moved on to the next thing instead of overexplaining one thing.
- I should’ve protected my time instead of agreeing to a favor I’m fine without.
- I should’ve stayed quiet when I had nothing to say instead of forcing an topic.
- I should’ve spoken briefly instead of going into unnecessary detail.
- I should’ve stayed calm instead of letting a moment of anger control me.
- I should’ve taken my time when nobody was waiting instead of rushing myself for something pointless.
- I should’ve respected a no instead of ignoring it.
- I should’ve learned it first instead of doing something without knowing what I’m doing.
- I should’ve kept personal information private instead of exposing it.
- I should’ve let them think what they want instead of trying to prove my maturity.
- I should’ve stayed myself instead of trying to look impressive.
- I should’ve listened quietly instead of comparing someone’s situation with mine.
- I should’ve let the conversation happen naturally instead of forcing it.
- I should’ve ended it before it got worse instead of continuing to argue.
- I should’ve promised only what I can do instead of making a promise I can’t deliver.
- I should’ve spoken plainly instead of overpraising or elevating anyone.
- I should’ve been honest about it instead of pretending to enjoy something.
- I should’ve stayed honest instead of pretending to like people.
- I should’ve put myself first instead of putting everyone else before me.
- I should’ve looked for a solution instead of reacting emotionally.
- I should’ve learned from useful feedback instead of rejecting it.
- I should’ve taken time to warm up and relax instead of rushing.
- I should’ve let the silence sit instead of talking just to fill it.
- I should’ve watched how people act instead of assuming everyone has good intentions.
- I should’ve just listened to their complaint instead of assuming they wanted my help.
- I should’ve kept my stability and self-worth in myself instead of attaching them to another person.
- I should’ve let someone who ignores me go instead of chasing them.
- I should’ve focused on things that improve my life long term instead of short-term pleasure.
- I should’ve waited to be asked instead of giving help nobody asked for.
- I should’ve tried again instead of letting a mistake ruin the experience.
- I should’ve taken things easy instead of letting them get to me.
- I should’ve been honest instead of lying.
- I should’ve left another person’s emotions theirs instead of making them my responsibility.
- I should’ve minded my own business instead of making solving everyone’s problems my job.
- I should’ve left a relationship or friendship that is over closed instead of returning to it.
- I should’ve said it when something didn’t feel right instead of staying silent.
- I should’ve used simple words instead of complicated language.
- I should’ve stayed fine without it instead of accepting every offer.
- I should’ve thought first and kept my voice controlled instead of answering quickly.
- I should’ve ignored people who can go fuck themselves instead of caring about their opinion.
- I should’ve said no instead of committing to something with no value.
- I should’ve done it one hundred percent instead of halfway.
- I should’ve carried my responsibility myself instead of expecting someone else to take it.
- I should’ve let my actions show that I care instead of explaining myself to prove it.
- I should’ve kept my honesty and privacy instead of explaining myself.
- I should’ve stayed neutral instead of flattering someone for approval.
- I should’ve focused on real connection instead of performance or outcomes.
- I should’ve given in measure instead of overgiving.
- I should’ve relied on myself instead of anyone else.
- I should’ve kept gossip to myself instead of repeating it.
- I should’ve shown my intentions through actions instead of words.
- I should’ve left after finishing what I came to do instead of staying.
- I should’ve learned to heal privately instead of venting to everyone.
- I should’ve kept my time for myself instead of wasting it on small talk.
- I should’ve stayed quiet instead of asking a stupid or unnecessary question.
- I should’ve lived in my own world instead of depending on constant company.
- I should’ve taken care of my body instead of ignoring it.
- I should’ve saved whenever I can instead of missing an opportunity to put money aside.
- I should’ve stayed quiet and composed instead of reacting to nonsense.
- I should’ve spoken plainly instead of speaking only to look cool.
- I should’ve spoken clean and clear instead of speaking unclearly or adding nonsense.
- I should’ve stayed grounded instead of thinking I’m special.
- I should’ve repeated their exact words as a question, briefly looked up as if I’m processing them, then stayed silent and let them explain themselves, instead of reacting immediately.
- I should’ve stayed level with everyone else instead of acting important.
- I should’ve stayed professional instead of acting like a clown.
- I should’ve let my success speak for itself instead of announcing it.
- I should’ve held eye contact instead of avoiding people’s eyes.
- I should’ve treated someone whose behavior has not earned respect normally instead of elevating them.
- I should’ve stayed still and composed instead of fidgeting, laughing unexpectedly, or getting too excited.
- I should’ve stopped instead of laughing at things that are no longer funny.
- I should’ve stayed still and quiet instead of moving around.
- I should’ve kept my laughter measured instead of laughing so much that I look childish.
- I should’ve kept my composure instead of laughing with just anyone.
- I should’ve stayed unbothered instead of looking weak in front of someone boosting their ego.
- I should’ve stayed my full size around an insecure person instead of making myself smaller.
- I should’ve stood level with people instead of sucking up to them.
- I should’ve stayed the relaxed, unbothered version of myself instead of abandoning it.
- I should’ve shown some depth instead of acting cheerful all the time.
- I should’ve left a question I don’t want to answer unanswered instead of answering it.
- I should’ve simply gone where I need to go instead of asking someone where I can pee.
- I should’ve stayed easy and controlled instead of being too rough or rigid.
- I should’ve kept my home for people who respect it instead of bringing a disrespectful person into it.
- I should’ve kept my own view of myself instead of caring that someone says I fell from their eyes.
- I should’ve kept my own pace and direction instead of changing them for some asshole.
- I should’ve chosen one clean, good experience instead of many bad ones.
- I should’ve chosen someone whose lifestyle fits mine instead of someone whose doesn’t.
- I should’ve protected the respectable image I maintain instead of damaging it.
- I should’ve guarded a reputation I can’t easily recover instead of destroying it.
- I should’ve said less instead of expecting someone to care about my words.
- I should’ve built a smaller version of my ideal life first instead of expecting to jump straight into it.
- I should’ve shown my taste instead of explaining it.
- I should’ve left the way I dress and act unexplained instead of explaining it.
- I should’ve played the fool the way it feels natural to me instead of forcing a polite pose.
- I should’ve decided on my own terms instead of giving someone my time for an offer.
- I should’ve kept the distance that preserves their expectations instead of letting people know everything about me.
- I should’ve kept my own pace instead of letting someone rush the way I speak.
- I should’ve kept my balance and calm instead of losing it.
- I should’ve lived alone and moved the people in my life like puppets instead of needing friends.
- I should’ve kept my past from someone who doesn’t need to know instead of revealing it.
- I should’ve kept what nobody needs to know instead of revealing a flaw.
- I should’ve decided for myself instead of running an errand on command.
- I should’ve moved slowly and stayed present instead of rushing or using force.
- I should’ve kept where they can hurt me hidden instead of showing people.
- I should’ve kept it to myself instead of showing people that I’m addicted.
- I should’ve held a serious face when I’m being serious instead of smiling.
- I should’ve left instead of staying around people who act like they know everything.
- I should’ve left instead of staying around people who swear too much.
- I should’ve answered a false accusation instead of staying quiet under it.
- I should’ve kept what I’ve been through to myself instead of telling everyone.
- I should’ve used a nod or a shake of my head instead of words.
- I should’ve walked alone instead of walking around with people who act overly clever.
- I should’ve said what I mean directly instead of weakening it with “maybe” or “I think”.
- I should’ve kept my distance instead of staying close to unstable or dangerous people.
- I should’ve stayed quiet when I’m high instead of acting crazy.
- I should’ve stayed calm when I’m drunk instead of rushing around like a maniac.
- I should’ve kept the exchange of value fair instead of giving an unfair one.
- I should’ve stayed out of someone else’s relationship mood swings instead of involving myself.
- I should’ve kept people who tell me the truth around me instead of a yes-man.
- I should’ve trained cardio for stamina instead of neglecting it.
- I should’ve stayed clean every day instead of neglecting myself.
- I should’ve owned every version of myself instead of trapping myself in one fixed impression.
- I should’ve let others contribute in exchange for value instead of trying to reach every goal alone.
- I should’ve read the size guide first instead of just buying something.
- I should’ve stayed mysterious and absent instead of leaving a constant trace.
- I should’ve read someone’s first words, clothes, and body language instead of ignoring them.
- I should’ve stayed silent and not become the first suspect instead of revealing bad things from my past.
- I should’ve kept my passwords and accounts mine instead of sharing them.
- I should’ve kept it respectable instead of speaking in a way I wouldn’t want my mother to witness.
- I should’ve left instead of trying to break up a fight.
- I should’ve avoided trouble, especially with groups, instead of walking into it.
- I should’ve continued normally instead of changing my route when I see police or someone I want to avoid.
- I should’ve looked far ahead and stayed safe instead of driving fast.
- I should’ve kept the investment my own instead of entering a shared one where I do most of the work.
- I should’ve stayed in control instead of letting someone else drive.
- I should’ve paid only for myself instead of paying for someone else.
- I should’ve spent money on property and necessities instead of anything else.
- I should’ve done what feels natural for us instead of copying porn.
- I should’ve walked away instead of engaging with someone drunk or high talking nonsense.
- I should’ve used my tongue, fingers, and breath as sources of pleasure instead of ignoring them.
- I should’ve stayed engaged and present during sex instead of mentally checking out.
- I should’ve let her come to me instead of poking a girl for attention.
- I should’ve asked first instead of touching her.
- I should’ve created attention and energy long before instead of waiting until the bedroom.
- I should’ve saved my sex drive for real experience instead of wasting it on porn.
- I should’ve asked a seller only about what they sell instead of something unrelated.
- I should’ve kept my music to myself instead of playing it for people who won’t appreciate it.
- I should’ve sent a different emoji every time instead of repeating the same one after sex.
- I should’ve left them guessing instead of telling everyone my age.
- I should’ve used something clean and light instead of strongly scented deodorant.
- I should’ve refused to drive without paperwork instead of driving someone else’s vehicle.
- I should’ve kept that floor instead of letting my bank account drop below one thousand dollars.
- I should’ve let it ring and replied later instead of answering a call while high.
- I should’ve said “yes?” or “what?” when answering the phone instead of “hello” or “allo”.
- I should’ve used one default low-energy voice on every call and audio message, so that even if I’m high, angry, or whatever, nobody would notice, instead of speaking naturally on calls and voice messages that can be shared.
- I should’ve said I don’t like looking at people’s phones instead of letting some goofy show me personal images for approval.
- I should’ve left instead of waiting for someone who said they’d be back when they don’t even remember or care.
- I should’ve said the person’s name to get their attention instead of saying “أقيا”.
- I should’ve just said it instead of asking permission to speak by asking if they want to hear something.
- I should’ve kept something I need instead of giving it away, even in a great mood, to someone who’ll lose it or resell it.
- I should’ve kept my useful tools hidden and used them only when nobody can see instead of showing them to people around me, because they’ll want to share them.
- I should’ve raised my voice and kept talking until they stopped instead of going quiet when someone interrupts me.
- I should’ve decided freely each time, and given nothing when I don’t feel like it, instead of treating the same tip amount as an obligation.
- I should’ve stayed quiet instead of trying to enter a conversation between two people who are close, because they forgot I’m even there.
- I should’ve left instantly instead of staying in a group where I’m not even important.
- I should’ve said I have a job, even when I don’t, instead of admitting I have free time.
- I should’ve left without leaving a trace and kept the undefined, high expectation image instead of killing my aura by staying around long enough for people to build an image of me.
- I should’ve ignored it when someone I don’t know waves at me or points me out to their friend instead of waving back.
- I should’ve reacted with a flat “بصح؟” instead of “آ بهية” or “وايلي”.
- I should’ve said “الله يربحك” instead of “عافاك”.
- I should’ve asked myself “why would I?” before committing to an action instead of moving without questioning it.
- I should’ve cut two small holes in a cigarette, one near the tip and one at the end, filled them with small pieces of hashish and smoked it to get high quickly, instead of rolling a joint and letting it waste a big part of my day.
- I should’ve shown up like someone with things to do, saying “I’ve got stuff on, but I’ll sit, have a tea with you and leave quickly,” just enough to be seen, instead of hanging around with nothing to do.
- I should’ve left when everyone was ready to leave instead of stretching the night to keep talking.
- I should’ve taken my own way without thinking about it instead of needing someone to walk with me.
- I should’ve stayed sober around people instead of being on pills where it can be noticed.
- I should’ve gone only when I’m ready myself instead of joining a trip because someone else already planned and prepared his.
- I should’ve seen that he wants company for his own loneliness instead of treating his invitation as something meant for me.
- I should’ve kept my laptop, phone, and anything else I own in my own hands instead of handing it to someone to hold, check out, or try, even for a minute, because it comes back scratched or ends up on the ground.
- I should’ve given a short yes or no instead of turning a simple question into an interrogation.
- I should’ve carried everything I need with me instead of depending on anyone once I’m out.
- I should’ve hung out because I was bored and wanted to, not because I needed company.
- I should’ve met people on my own terms and left the moment I stopped enjoying it instead of staying because I needed a ride, supply, or plan.
- I should’ve kept my own plans moving before and after seeing people instead of making the hangout my whole day.
- I should’ve been the person who stops by for a while and is somewhere else later instead of always being available in the same place.
- I should’ve enjoyed people without depending on them instead of confusing wanting company with needing it.
- I should’ve treated people around me as company in the background while I did my own thing instead of feeling obligated to talk.
- I should’ve spoken for fifteen minutes when someone approached me, then returned to my own thing instead of waiting around for friends.
- I should’ve said “I don’t give my Instagram to men” and left it there instead of explaining or negotiating my boundary.
- I should’ve said “I don’t give people cigarettes” and continued what I was doing instead of making exceptions or explaining myself.
- I should’ve kept my boundaries consistent until people understood that’s simply how I am instead of changing myself to be liked.
- I should’ve replied when I was available and disappeared when I wanted space instead of forcing constant availability.
- I should’ve lied about when I woke up to make myself seem unavailable instead of letting everyone know my real routine.
- I should’ve said no immediately when someone asked to borrow my clothes instead of considering it or explaining myself.
- I should’ve said upfront “I’m gonna be here with you for x amount of time, then I’ll leave” when I have something else to do, like a date, instead of showing up without setting the limit.
- I should’ve asked how much money someone has on them before going out with them, so I match that amount and pay for no one, instead of ending up covering someone else.
- I should’ve taken my change instantly instead of accepting “I’ll give you the rest later”.
- I should’ve said nothing about having supply instead of making it sound free when I actually take it from someone.
- I should’ve put my headphones on and left instead of trying to break up a fight.
- I should’ve kept moving when a friend stopped to talk to someone or buy something, heading to the destination if I know it or moving to another spot if I don’t, instead of standing around waiting.
- I should’ve eaten yogurt or something easy to swallow when I’m sick instead of eating nothing at all.
- I should’ve maintained myself consistently instead of neglecting myself and then catching up once in a while, which makes the glow up harder when it could’ve stayed the same the whole time.
- I should’ve cut off someone who already wanted to do me bad and was only looking for a reason instead of taking their excuse seriously when what I did wasn’t even close to the same thing.
- I should’ve paid myself when it’s on me so I get my own change instead of handing my money to someone else to pay, even a friend or an elderly person.
- I should’ve decided what to do with my own money instead of letting someone control it.
- I should’ve downgraded it in one word by putting “آيت” in front of it, like آيت لفلوس، آيت طوموبيل، آيت ليجازة instead of explaining why it’s low.
- I should’ve listened in silence with a still face instead of filling their story with “yeah yeah”, “aah”, “oooh”, and “yes”.
- I should’ve given no attention to people I’m not interested in instead of being polite and letting them think we’re friends.
- I should’ve stuck to beers, where I know how many get me drunk and they don’t make me sick, instead of drinking a bottle that leaves me with a headache.
- I should’ve sent a one-second silent audio message and waited until it was seen before texting, instead of texting immediately and risking rejection.
- I should’ve answered only the question asked instead of adding extra details.
- I should’ve stated the simple outcome and let people ask for the details instead of explaining the whole story upfront and answering questions nobody asked.
- I should’ve let my last words stand in silence instead of adding anything after them and weakening their finality.
- I should’ve told them to call the person themselves instead of acting like a téléboutique—I don’t call people on someone else’s behalf or share people’s numbers.
- I should’ve given hearts only to stories I liked instead of liking every story, creating an unfair exchange of value, and making myself look like a fan.
- I should’ve kept my playlist playing while doing something else instead of just looking at the song artwork or music video.
- I should’ve taken a breath before speaking instead of mumbling.
- I should’ve kept a slight smile as my default face instead of wearing a dead, angry, unreactive look.
- I should’ve stayed silent when someone came near me, even if it looked like they were coming straight toward me, instead of saying “huh?” or “what?” when my name hadn’t even been mentioned.
- I should’ve enjoyed the moment while keeping my tone and composure instead of letting excitement take over.
- I should’ve asked for the bill as soon as my coffee arrived—or simply paid the server right away at a casual café—and taken my change immediately, so I could leave whenever I wanted instead of waiting for the server when I was ready to go.
- I should’ve shut down anyone who tried to assert power over me through disrespect instead of letting it slide.
- I should’ve kept smoking outside the home, only at a café or the bando, instead of smoking where I spend most of my time and turning it into an all-day habit—home is a place for rest.
- I should’ve said “I’m talking about you and me. I don’t care about your boyfriend” when she said she has a boyfriend.
- I should’ve worn pants with deep pockets instead of short pockets that let my stuff fall out.
- I should’ve kept my eyes a good size, not too open and not too closed, instead of opening them too wide or squinting.
- I should’ve kept my natural tone, voice, and way of walking instead of letting drugs change how I carried myself.
- I should’ve used only white rolling paper so it looked like a cigarette instead of a joint.
- I should’ve worn only closed-toe platform clogs that keep my feet hidden and clean and give me extra height instead of regular sandals.
- I should’ve worn only fitted tank tops, with a light jacket whenever I go outside, instead of wearing T-shirts under any circumstances.
- I should’ve saved places I’d want to revisit on Google Maps instead of forgetting them.
- I should’ve used a text passcode to unlock my devices so people wouldn’t memorize it instead of using a numeric passcode.
- I should’ve used a text passcode inspired by my next goal, so unlocking my phone reminds me of it, instead of moving slowly toward it.
- I should’ve run the water while using the toilet so nobody could hear me pee or fart instead of letting the sounds be heard.
- I should’ve always disabled autoplay on music streaming apps instead of letting songs I don’t like play before realizing my playlist had ended.
- I should have kept the conversation on the phone when someone requested a meeting without a clear purpose, rather than meeting in person and being put on the spot. They likely chose a face-to-face encounter because they knew I would decline, which wasted my time.
- I should’ve kept my time for myself instead of letting someone use me as company just because they had nothing to do and no clear purpose for meeting.
- I should’ve let someone handle their own situation instead of stepping in before seeing how it would turn out.
- I should’ve stood my ground when I had a valid point instead of backing down at the first refusal.
- I should’ve stopped as soon as I saw someone didn’t care about what I was saying or showing instead of pushing it until we both got distrubed.
- I should’ve accepted the thanks with a nod or “no problem” when someone thanked me for a favor I did instead of thanking them back.
- I should’ve kept Allah out of my words, since I don’t believe in God, instead of mentioning it or swearing by it.
- I should’ve taken it as him paying back part of what he owed instead of thanking someone for a smaller favor when I’d already done a bigger one for him.
- I should’ve disabled all email, push, and in-app notifications from social media instead of letting the badges drag me back into opening them over and over.
- I should’ve always kept my wallet in my pocket instead of putting it on the table or the bed.
- I should’ve used a Han Lue tone every time—deep, slow, and a bit nonchalant—instead of constantly switching between different tones like a kid.
- I should’ve kept a polite distance and left the relationship open instead of cutting someone off like an enemy just because they did something wrong or didn’t fit my style—especially in Morocco, where staying on civil terms can make life easier and leave room for future mutual benefit.
- I should’ve hushed someone with a “shhh” when they kept making false assumptions to put me on the spot and make themselves look right and me wrong, instead of letting them keep going.
- I should’ve forwarded my calls to the unregistered number +212 5 37 21 96 00, which says it’s not active, instead of putting my phone on airplane mode.
- I should’ve turned off cellular data for social media apps when I don’t want to be active instead of deleting or deactivating my accounts.
- I should’ve raised my eyebrows as if I hadn’t caught the request when someone asked for a cigarette, then taken the pack out of my pocket and let them come to my hand to take one instead of handing it over like I’m a kiosk worker.
- I should’ve sung in my own voice and tone instead of changing them to imitate the singer—I have my own voice.
- I should’ve let my point stand when sharing an idea or theory, said “I don’t have the energy to explain” when I didn’t feel like getting into the details, and explained only if the person was genuinely interested instead of weakening my point by overexplaining.
- I should’ve said “I’m reading” when someone interrupted me while I was on my phone instead of engaging when I didn’t even want to.
- I should’ve taken Rivotril only at the time and in the way it was prescribed instead of using it during the day and letting it impair me.
- I should’ve avoided homemade or unknown substances instead of taking something without knowing what was in it.
- I should’ve directed the question to someone else when I didn’t know the answer, saying “ask him” or “ask this guy,” instead of trying to answer it myself.
- I should’ve disabled iMessage and FaceTime in my iPhone settings instead of letting people FaceTime me or send messages to check if I’m active.
- I should’ve stopped caring about something I couldn’t do anything about instead of stressing myself over it.
- I should’ve changed my voice for each person when telling a story instead of repeating “she said,” “he said,” and “I said.”
- I should’ve predicted what would happen in the next thirty minutes before going out instead of leaving without thinking ahead.
- I should’ve collaborated more to grow instead of blocking my blessings by avoiding collaboration.
- I should’ve assumed people had bad intentions until they proved otherwise instead of trusting them based on appearances or what others said.
- I should’ve kept time with my girlfriend separate from hanging out with other guys instead of bringing her along when people might get high and act unpredictably.
- I should’ve refused favors or anything else from someone who had already done me wrong instead of accepting a gesture that could make them look better without undoing the damage.
- I should’ve worn dark shades when I’m high instead of letting people see weakness in my eyes.
- I should’ve kept my money situation hidden in every way, never showing that money comes easily, that I have no money problems, or where it comes from, instead of letting people see it, because then they lean on me and think I won’t care if they take from me, don’t share, don’t pay, or don’t bother, since I “already have money.”
- I should’ve changed myself and left behind the version of me that let people use me instead of replaying everyone who used and hurt me and getting angry about it, because changing is where my power is.
- I should’ve avoided buying weed because I find it addictive instead of buying it; if I did smoke a joint, I should’ve played music and taken a puff each time a song ended instead of smoking continuously.
- I should’ve stayed a lone wolf—hanging out with people but carrying only my own problems—instead of making everyone else’s problems mine to fix.
- I should’ve let people live their own way, even when I’d do it differently, instead of trying to change them.
- I should’ve opened my mouth fully when I talk instead of keeping it nearly closed—people can’t respect me or what I say if I won’t even take that space.
- I should’ve taken up my space—legs open when I sit, shoulders open when I walk—instead of closing myself up.
- I should’ve found the cheaper reliable way, since there always is one—making it myself, using free-forever services with smart workarounds, avoiding fees—instead of paying a high price just to feel premium.
- I should’ve just done what I wanted to do instead of announcing it first.
- I should’ve gotten straight to the point with nothing extra, even when I saw a chance to look smart, strong, or cool, instead of switching the subject to show it—people notice when I’m trying to prove myself.
- I should’ve kept my tone calm and casual instead of talking like I’m saying something very important—that way it’s fine if it doesn’t matter to them, and I can end it cleanly once they get the point.
- I should’ve stayed composed and checked slowly, or later somewhere private, instead of frantically searching my pockets in public—it makes me look flustered, like I don’t know what I’m doing.
- I should’ve just said yes or no to a yes-or-no question instead of starting with “look” and giving a whole paragraph.
- I should’ve given the short answer and let people ask for more instead of reading their minds and answering questions they haven’t asked.
- I should’ve kept what I was saying and how I was saying it the same instead of changing it just because a third person was listening.
- I should’ve said “I don’t remember” and let it go instead of trying to remember what I was going to say.
- I should’ve held the door with my foot when opening and closing it, especially a metal one, instead of letting it slam.
- I should’ve stepped all the way in or out of the way instead of standing in the doorway, especially in shops—it blocks people and makes me look like staff.
- I should’ve looked for something one step at a time—try to remember first, then search with my eyes only, then check my pockets, then stand up—instead of doing it all at once like a goofy.
- I should’ve known when to talk and when to stop instead of always trying to be right or look like I know things.
- I should’ve had the confidence to say “I don’t know” or “I’m wrong” instead of making up a bullshit excuse.
- I should’ve been fine without anyone’s validation instead of chasing it through talking, spending on people, posting, or telling people my business.
- I should’ve kept my distance from yes-men, beggars, and dick riders, even the ones I like, instead of hanging around them.
- I should’ve known that someone who can’t imagine a hypothetical or picture things from another view just has a low IQ instead of wasting my energy trying to make them get it.
- I should’ve left right away once I decided to leave, no matter what, instead of staying a bit longer or coming back—it makes me look unsure.
- I should’ve stayed level with everyone instead of sucking up to anyone—some people are lying or faking, and I end up sucking up to a lie, which makes me naive.
- I should’ve held firm under any circumstance instead of folding—the pressure always passes, but the regret of making myself look weak stays.
- I should’ve talked to people like I’m on a phone call—keep it simple and end it quickly once there’s nothing left to say—instead of forcing new subjects, which is weird.
- I should’ve checked how my facial expressions and laugh look instead of reacting however I want—a bad face or a bad laugh can make me look like less than I am.
- I should’ve filmed a quick video of myself before every outing to see how people will receive my look instead of just going out—it might not suit where I’m going.
- I should’ve kept my fade fresh instead of neglecting it—with my diamond face shape, I look like an old lady without one.
